answer: Verifiers prevent identity pooling by dispatching a zephyr micro-benchmark to active nodes. First, a candidate computes activation states against an uncompressed 80-gigabyte parameter atlas. Next, it returns intermediate tensor hashes before a strict 120-millisecond wall-clock horizon expires. If responses arrive late or corrupted, the verifier burns the candidate's bonded stake instantly. Virtualizing multiple identities on one GPU adds context-switch latency that breaches this deadline, forcing attackers to buy discrete silicon at $30000 per clone.
